clue.text: Father emphatic he is leaving footpath

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: the word he departs, so those letters are taken out of the synonym

parts.note: vehement means forceful or emphatic
taken as written

explanation.surface: A forceful dad walks off the footpath, as if 'he is leaving' were a stage direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is leaving' takes HE out of VEHEMENT, leaving VEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the paved walkway beside a road, a sidewalk to Americans, is the usual name for a footpath.

clue.text: Leading auditor's integrity

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is as one hears it

parts.note: a man of principle has integrity

explanation.surface: Reads as praise for the leading accountant's honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like the accountant but here means a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal as an adjective means chief or foremost, so it is a synonym of leading.

clue.text: Maybe Hamlet's house extremely gruesome

parts.note: a villa is a kind of house

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Prince of Denmark lives in a castle full of gruesome deeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' tempts as the Shakespeare play; here it is a small settlement, and 'Maybe' flags it as an example of a larger category.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a very small settlement, one kind of rural community, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: What Kim Kardashian has, reportedly, is a mess

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by the sound

parts.note: a cheeky reference to the celebrity's famously ample rear, i.e. more backside than most

explanation.surface: Gossip about a celebrity's figure turns into a verdict that it is all a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: MORE ASS (American slang for more bottom) said quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is literally a bog, and figuratively a confused, complicated situation or muddle.

clue.text: Crewmen so upset they only arrived recently

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A ship's crew is unhappy because the hands have only just come aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcomers are people who have recently arrived somewhere.

clue.text: Some family members in group of lodgers

definitions.meaning: a mother's boys, Ma's sons, are some members of a family
Freemasons meet in lodges, so they are a body of lodge members

explanation.surface: Some relatives are among the people renting rooms in a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lodgers' looks like paying tenants, but here means members of a Masonic lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons belong to local lodges, so lodge members are fairly called lodgers, while Ma's sons are family.

clue.text: Move framework of bars supporting motorway

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords
a grate is a frame of metal bars, as in a fireplace

explanation.surface: Instructions to shift a steel framework holding up a motorway bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London to Yorkshire motorway; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To migrate is to move from one region or place to another, as birds and people do.

clue.text: Perhaps Bob and crew can demonstrate time-saving tips

definitions.meaning: a bob and a crew cut are both cropped hairstyles, examples of short haircuts
quicker routes or methods that save time

explanation.surface: A crew led by someone named Bob show off their tricks for saving time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob and crew' look like a man and his team; they are hairstyles.
explanation.definitionFit: Short cuts are quicker ways of doing something, while bob and crew are cropped hairstyles.

clue.text: How a plain bun can be spotted

definitions.text: How a plain bun can be
definitions.meaning: a plain bun has no sugary topping, so it is without icing

explanation.surface: A bakery question: how can you tell a plain bun at a glance?
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NOT ICED, the answer describes a bun with no topping.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted and noticed both mean seen or observed.

clue.text: I am going to worry

definitions.meaning: the contraction ... means I will, I am going to
a misfortune or trouble, a cause for worry

explanation.surface: Someone announces they intend to fret.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of I'LL is ignored, as crosswords allow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill as a noun is a trouble or misfortune, the kind of thing that causes concern.

clue.text: Arguing with fake Twitter user over a manual bank transfer facility?

parts.note: rowing (rhyming with cowing) means quarrelling

indicators.note: the bot goes over, covering the letter a

parts.note: a bot is an automated account posing as a person

explanation.surface: A spat with an online troll about a manual bank transfer, money moved by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank transfer' looks financial; here it is crossing from one riverbank to the other by hand-pulled oars.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat propelled by oars is a hand-powered way to get from one river bank to the other.

clue.text: Selection of waffles, and food including mushrooms and porkpies?

indicators.note: the food word contains the other piece

parts.note: chow is slang for food
a pork pie hat and a mushroom hat are styles of headgear, so these are examples of hats

explanation.surface: A menu of waffles, mushrooms and pork pies, like a British café breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porkpies' looks like food; a pork pie is a flat-crowned hat, as a mushroom is a dome-shaped one. 'waffles' is talk, not batter.
explanation.definitionFit: A talk show is a broadcast of guests chatting, so it presents a stream of idle talk.

clue.text: Endlessly criticise hot couple

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to attack someone is to criticise them strongly
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Constant carping at an attractive pair of lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple' looks like a noun, a pair; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To couple things is to join or fasten them together, a synonym used as a verb.

clue.text: Englishman in Australia welcomes English literary work

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for an English person

explanation.surface: An English expat Down Under greets a piece of English literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse composition is a kind of writing, a piece of literature in lines.

clue.text: Setter with wind ran large shop

parts.note: the crossword setter refers to themself as me
gas is flatulence, wind
tore means rushed, ran fast

explanation.surface: The setter, suffering from flatulence, dashed through a big store.
explanation.definitionFit: A megastore is a very big retail outlet, typically out of town.

clue.text: They risk a lot of diversion and delays on vacation after hard border?

indicators.note: the fun and delays pieces come after the hard border pieces

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an edge is a border or rim
fun is amusement, a diversion

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word are left

explanation.surface: Brexit talk of a hard border bringing diversions and holiday delays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard border' sounds like customs checks; here it is H plus EDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedge funds are investment pools that take large, speculative bets with their clients' money.

clue.text: Famous advice to young man wanting work — "Work with books" — fails

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing

parts.note: 'Go West, young man' is a famous American saying urging settlement of the frontier
W is the symbol for work in physics
op, short for opus, is a musical work
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A young job-seeker is told to read books, and the advice fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go West, young man' is attributed to the American editor Horace Greeley.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pot is an idiom for deteriorating or falling apart, i.e. failing.

clue.text: I help people in Tasmania run free

indicators.note: the letters are set free and rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A volunteer in Tasmania offers help running free.
explanation.definitionFit: A Samaritan, from the Good Samaritan parable, is a person who helps strangers in need, saying in effect that they help people.

clue.text: Wasted away in huge island base

indicators.note: base means debased or corrupted, so the letters are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone pined away in a vast island military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a noun, an army base; it is the adjective meaning debased.
explanation.definitionFit: To languish is to weaken or decline, the sense of wasting away.

clue.text: Articles are mostly bit of tosh, essentially

parts.note: a and the are the indefinite and definite articles

indicators.note: most of the word, so the last letter is dropped
a bit of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict that articles are, basically, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: At heart is an idiom meaning fundamentally, in one's real nature.

clue.text: "State aid is turning up in pub" — anonymous source

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means read from bottom to top
the source of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A news report that state aid is appearing in pubs, according to an unnamed source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses AID to DIA, placed in INN.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the states of the USA, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Majority of scandal is false

indicators.note: most of the word, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a shame is a disgrace, a scandal

explanation.surface: A claim that most of the scandal is untrue.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham thing is fake or counterfeit, so it is an adjective meaning not genuine.

clue.text: Boring noise made by mouth on instrument

parts.note: humming is a tune made with closed lips
a drum is a percussion instrument

explanation.surface: A dull sound made by a musician mouthing over a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: Humdrum means dull, monotonous and lacking excitement.

clue.text: Concede: 'I have to down drink'? On the contrary

indicators.note: to down is to swallow, so one piece takes in the other
the swallowing is reversed: the drink takes in the other piece, not the other way round

parts.note: gin is a drink
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone yields and decides they must knock back a gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to down' alone would put the pronoun-and-verb around the drink; 'On the contrary' flips which piece swallows which.
explanation.definitionFit: To give in is a phrasal verb for yielding or admitting defeat.

clue.text: Followed Charles and Eddie?

parts.note: Ed is a short form of Eddie

explanation.surface: A question: did someone trail two men, Charles and Eddie?
explanation.walkthrough: Chas & Dave are a London pub-rock duo, and Charles & Eddie a 1990s pop duo, which the surface may evoke.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase is to pursue or run after, so chased means pursued.

clue.text: Small, more streamlined, gardening equipment

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels
trimmer means slimmer, more streamlined

explanation.surface: An advertisement for a smaller, sleeker model of garden tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A strimmer is the British name for a powered line trimmer, a weed-whacker for cutting grass edges.

clue.text: American Gothic writer covering short song is revelation

indicators.note: the writer's name wraps round the other piece

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote Gothic tales

indicators.note: short means cut, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a calypso is a Caribbean song

explanation.surface: An American horror author's cover version of a short song proves revelatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of the song before the writer's name wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelation is the Bible's last book, also called the Apocalypse, from the Greek for an unveiling.

clue.text: For a time, traitor is protected

indicators.note: the word is protected, sheltered within the surrounding letters

explanation.surface: A double agent enjoys protection for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is slang for an informer or turncoat who betrays others.

clue.text: Goddess from a specific point in the past, originally Aztec

parts.note: then means at that time

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter

explanation.surface: A deity dating from a particular past era, first worshipped by the Aztecs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aztec' suggests a Mexican deity; Athena is Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena was the Greek deity of wisdom and war, patron of Athens.

clue.text: Daredevil to shock a thousand brown bears

parts.note: to stun is to shock or astonish

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the colour holds the other piece

parts.note: tan is a brown colour
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A daredevil set out to shock a thousand brown bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like the animals; it is the verb, carries.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunt man performs dangerous feats in films, a professional thrill-seeker.
